question: What should I check before leaving for an Erasmus exchange?
expected_key_points: Wait for the Outgoing Mobility Office email before starting the host university application.
Respect the host university application deadlines.
Complete a Learning Agreement of at least 30 ECTS and obtain the required signatures.
Complete the OLS language evaluation if the teaching language is not the student's mother tongue.
Complete the required enrolment steps and upload the signed mobility contract through the mobility portal.
Arrange accommodation and check health insurance, passport validity and visa requirements.
answer:
Before leaving for an Erasmus exchange, you should check the following items as stated in the official documentation:

- Check your passport validity and visa requirements, as some partners require validity beyond your mobility period (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Check that your European health insurance card is valid for the whole mobility period (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Download the International SOS assistance app, and follow the instructions received via email (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Luxembourgish students should report their trip to the MAEE for safety reasons (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

The provided source text does not cover what other specific personal checks might be required beyond these points.

question: Which documents should I prepare for Erasmus registration?
expected_key_points: Prepare a Learning Agreement (LA or OLA) covering at least 30 ECTS.
Obtain the required signatures from the student, programme director and host institution.
Upload the signed mobility contract through the mobility portal.
Complete the OLS language evaluation if the teaching language is not the student's mother tongue.
answer:
Based on the official sources provided, the University of Luxembourg does not explicitly detail a document list labeled specifically for "Erasmus registration" as a single entry. However, the sources mention several compulsory documents and forms that students must prepare or submit before and during their mobility:

- Grant Agreement / Mobility Contract: A compulsory administrative document containing mobility information and grant details that must be signed and uploaded via the mobility portal (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Learning Agreement (LA) or Online Learning Agreement (OLA), and any changes made via the "Changes to learning agreement" form if the host university does not use the online form (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Valid European health insurance card (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Documents required for the "fewer opportunities" top-up, depending on the case (a doctor-completed form provided by the University, a household composition certificate and proof that children spent the mobility period abroad, or a residence permit indicating refugee status) (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

The provided source text does not cover a comprehensive checklist specifically titled "Erasmus registration." Please consult the University's Erasmus+ guidance or contact the relevant mobility office (Outgoing Mobility Office / BRI, bri.outgoing@uni.lu) for any further details (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: How can I check whether my courses will transfer as credits?
expected_key_points: Agree on the courses and their recognition through the Learning Agreement.
Use the Learning Agreement to record the courses and ECTS.
If courses change during mobility, update the Learning Agreement using Table A2.
Provide reasons for exceptional course changes.
Obtain the required signatures from the student, host institution and sending institution.
Credits agreed in the Learning Agreement and confirmed by the Transcript of Records are automatically recognised according to the form.
answer:
To check whether your courses will transfer as credits, you must complete a Learning Agreement (or Online Learning Agreement) listing your provisional courses at the host university. This agreement must first be approved by your home study programme director and then by your host institution. By signing the Learning Agreement, your home university agrees to validate the credits upon your return if the courses are completed successfully.

The official sources do not cover what happens if you fail to complete the Learning Agreement process before undertaking your courses. 

To ensure credit transfer, the latest and approved version of your Learning Agreement must correspond to the Transcript of Records provided by the host university at the end of your mobility. Only credits from courses approved on the final Learning Agreement are validated. 

Sources:
- https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/ (Last checked: 14.11.2026)
- https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026)
- https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026)

question: How should I plan health insurance for studying abroad in Europe?
expected_key_points: Arrange adequate health insurance before travelling.
Know that International SOS provides free 24/7 assistance for mobility trips.
Understand that International SOS is not an insurance provider and does not replace health insurance.
answer:
To plan health insurance for studying abroad in Europe, you should check that your European health insurance card (CNS) is valid for the whole stay abroad. 

The official sources do not cover additional specific planning steps beyond checking the validity of your European health insurance card (CNS) for stays in Europe. For other regions outside Europe, supplementary health, travel, and repatriation insurance are required.

question: Which deadlines should I put in an Erasmus preparation checklist?
expected_key_points: Regularly check the university student email account for mobility instructions.
Ensure the European Health Insurance Card is valid before departure.
After arrival, obtain the signed and stamped Certificate of Arrival and upload it to the mobility portal.
Update the Learning Agreement within the first month after arrival if courses or ECTS change.
At the end of the exchange, obtain and upload the Certificate of End of Stay and the required Learning Agreement documents.
Complete the online mobility report.
After returning, provide the required Transcript of Records to the academic contact.
answer:
According to the official sources, there are no specific calendar deadline dates published for an Erasmus preparation checklist (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305, Last checked: 14.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

However, the sources provide the following relative timing guidelines that you can use:
- Prepare for your mobility semester one academic year before departure (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- The Study Abroad Day info session takes place each year in November, on the second Thursday (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- Sign the mobility contract before departure or during the first month of mobility (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Update the learning agreement within the month of arrival if there are changes in courses or ECTS (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- The first payment of the Erasmus+ grant (70%) is received a minimum of 4 weeks after receipt of your mobility contract with your signature via the mobility portal, and the balance is paid at least 4 weeks after receipt of the compulsory end-of-stay documents (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

The official sources do not cover specific calendar dates for application deadlines. Host universities may also set their own deadlines (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
